exposure: maternal ability to recognize emotions (specifically fear)
maternal group (at-risk-of postpartum psychosis vs. healthy controls)
cohort: The study included 98 women and their offspring, consisting of 40 women at-risk-of postpartum psychosis (diagnosed with Bipolar Disorder, Schizoaffective Disorder, or previous PP) and 58 healthy controls.
finding: Maternal inability to recognize fear predicted lower quality mother-infant interaction at 8 weeks and 12 months postpartum, independent of maternal group, while infant social-interactive behavior at birth also predicted mother-infant interaction at 12 months.
